title: Grain-silo farmer stockpiles helium, quartz and tungsten in strategic reserve
idea: Persona: a farmer who stores grain against drought. Create a U.S. critical-fab-input reserve holding 18-24 months of helium (stored in depleted gas fields), synthetic quartz crucibles, W powder and WF6, neon and fluorochemicals. Finance it with a small fee per wafer start and release stock only above a price trigger.
why: Turns supply shocks, such as the Qatar helium outage or Chinese tungsten export controls, into price ripples instead of fab stoppages.

title: Anodized mesoporous silicon electrodes multiply capacitor area
idea: TRIZ #31 Porous materials: anodize heavily doped silicon electrode arms in HF to form 3-5 nm mesopores, line the pores with ALD Al2O3/TiO2 nanolaminate, and fill them with TiN, so each electrode becomes a sponge with ~3-10x the surface area.
why: Reaches the needed Cs at an aspect ratio of ~20:1 instead of ~70:1, or makes lateral 3D-DRAM capacitors ~3x shorter, with no exotic high-k (Si, Al, Ti, N, O, F only).

title: Urban-mined DRAM: re-binned retired DIMM dies in CXL expanders
idea: Box [existing DDR4 die | existing access | existing sense | CXL Type-3 expander | retired server DIMMs | test + retention re-binning]: route decommissioned hyperscale DIMMs to a test line that sorts dies by retention and bit-error rate, then a CXL controller with strong ECC and per-bin refresh tuning presents them as pooled far memory.
why: Raises usable memory supply with zero new wafers, crucibles, helium or tungsten; millions of retired DIMMs per year become a far-memory tier that offsets new DDR5 demand.

title: Po the array is a hologram: interference-lithography cell arrays
idea: Po: 'the memory array is a hologram.' Extracted: expose the periodic array layers (active lines, wordlines, bitlines) by two- and four-beam interference of a 1990s frequency-quadrupled 266 nm laser, printing ~150 nm-pitch gratings over a whole 200 mm wafer at once; a KrF stepper then trims at mat edges and patterns the periphery.
why: Litho capital and masks: array layers need no reticle and no scanner time, at roughly 2x finer pitch than the stepper alone, with U.S.-buildable optics.

title: Pre-formed porous cleave layer makes CZ wafers reusable donors
idea: TRIZ #10 Prior action: before any device processing, anodize a double-porosity silicon layer into a prime CZ wafer and grow 3-5 um of device-grade epitaxial silicon on top (ELTRAN-style). After the array front-end, the wafer is bonded to a carrier or periphery wafer and cleaved at the porous layer, and the donor is re-polished and reused 10-20 times.
why: The DRAM active layer is a few um of a 775 um wafer, so this cuts CZ ingot, polysilicon energy and HPQ crucible use per wafer by ~5-10x.

title: Laser-sliced HBM wafer bodies reused as bonding carrier wafers
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation through the thickness: instead of grinding away 700 um, focus a sub-bandgap infrared laser ~80 um below the device side to write a modified plane (as KABRA does for SiC), then split the wafer. The ~650 um body is re-polished and reused as the temporary carrier wafer that HBM thinning and TSV reveal already require.
why: Halves virgin silicon demand on HBM lines (device wafer plus carrier) and removes most of the grinding time, wheel wear and slurry water.

title: Swiss-roll capacitors: strained films self-roll into nano-scrolls
idea: Like a wound film capacitor or a jelly roll, deposit a TiN/dielectric/TiN stack on a strained bilayer over a sacrificial layer; releasing it makes the film curl into a tight multi-turn scroll above each cell, multiplying plate area 10-20x with no deep hole etch.
why: Gives 2-5x more Cs per footprint than 70:1 pillars while eliminating the high-AR fluorocarbon etch and its multilayer hard mask (PFAS gas, energy and critical litho for the hole layer).

title: All-oxide CMOS periphery lets memory panels need no silicon chips
idea: Ideal: periphery made from the same cheap film as the cells. Closest: build sense amps, decoders and refresh logic from complementary oxide TFTs (n-ZnSnO with p-SnO or p-Cu2O, all abundant, <=300 C) using bootstrapped dynamic logic to compensate the weak p-FET, so panel memory needs no bonded silicon driver ICs.
why: 100x enabler: periphery is ~49% of DRAM die (Fact 7); moving it onto ~$30/m2 panel layers is required to reach ~$0.1/GB. Trades sensing speed (50-200 ns) and power.

title: Leather tanner's chrome green: voltage-written chromia magnetoelectric memory
idea: Persona: a tanner who works with chromium oxide, the chrome green pigment. Boron-doped Cr2O3 is a room-temperature magnetoelectric antiferromagnet, so a voltage pulse with a small bias field reverses its boundary magnetization. An exchange-coupled Fe/MgO/Fe junction reads the state.
why: Non-volatile memory written by voltage instead of current, at fJ-class energy, with no Pt, Ir or Co.

title: Vertical Bloch-line memory revived in rare-earth-free barium hexaferrite
idea: Revive Konishi's 1983 vertical-Bloch-line memory, which stores bits as pairs of Bloch lines inside stripe-domain walls, in perpendicular BaFe12O19 hexaferrite (Ba and Fe are abundant) instead of gadolinium-gallium garnets. A 1 um i-line pattern hosts bits about 10x finer than itself.
why: No EUV, yet bit density below the lithography limit; nonvolatile; no Gd, Ga, Hf or W; claims 10-30x density over the litho node used, as a nonvolatile memory tier.

title: Painter's Prussian blue pigment becomes a non-volatile ionic memory
idea: Persona: a painter whose Prussian blue (iron hexacyanoferrate) is also a sodium-ion battery cathode. Build a three-terminal ECRAM in which gate pulses shuttle Na+ between a Prussian-white reservoir and a Prussian-blue channel, setting its conductance. Read is separate from write and non-destructive.
why: Non-volatile and lithium-free, made of Fe, C, N and Na. The non-destructive read avoids DRAM's destructive read (fact 8).

title: Substitute self-forming manganese silicate barriers for tantalum liners
idea: Plate periphery copper on a Cu-Mn alloy seed; on anneal Mn segregates to the dielectric interface and forms a 1-2 nm MnSixOy barrier, eliminating PVD TaN/Ta liners.
why: Removes conflict-mineral tantalum and frees ~3-4 nm of each narrow wire for copper, lowering periphery wire resistance and energy per bit moved.

title: Plumber lines copper wordlines with a self-forming manganese barrier
idea: Persona: a plumber who lines ordinary copper pipe instead of buying exotic pipe. Fill buried-wordline trenches with Cu-2%Mn alloy. On anneal, the Mn migrates to the dielectric interface and forms a ~1.5 nm MnSiOx diffusion barrier, so no thick TiN/W stack is needed and copper fills the whole trench.
why: Removes tungsten from wordlines, the largest W use in the array. Cu resistivity is 1.7 versus 5.3 uOhm-cm for W, so wordline RC falls ~2-3x and longer wordlines need less periphery.

title: Moonshine stills for helium: modular skids on stranded U.S. wells
idea: Like a moonshiner's portable still, skid-mounted membrane and pressure-swing helium purifiers sit on low-volume Kansas, Montana and Arizona gas and nitrogen wells that big plants ignore, filling ISO cryo-containers run on a milk route to U.S. fabs under long-term offtake contracts.
why: Builds a fab-dedicated domestic helium supply independent of Qatar and the large-plant oligopoly; each skid adds ~5-30 Mcf/day, so a few dozen can cover a large DRAM fab.

title: Precursor boomerang: recycled lower-purity ALD precursors
idea: Reverse precursor flow: cold-trap the ~90% of unreacted Zr/Hf/Ti amides from ALD exhaust, resynthesize them on site to ~4N instead of 6N, and accept the resulting trace-impurity leaky cells within the 1% BER budget.
why: Cuts virgin hafnium/zirconium precursor demand ~5x and specialty-chemical supply dependence.

title: Acid-leached rice-husk silica as high-purity crucible feedstock
idea: TRIZ #27 Cheap short-living objects: the crucible is single-use anyway, so source its silica from a cheap renewable stream. Leach rice husks with HCl/oxalic acid to strip K, Ca and Fe, burn them under controlled oxidation to amorphous SiO2, chlorine-purify the ash at ~1000 C, and arc-fuse it into crucible inner layers.
why: Diversifies HPQ away from Spruce Pine using U.S. Gulf-coast husk (~0.3 Mt/yr of silica available), targeting 5N purity at below mined-HPQ cost. Uses only Si, O, Cl, C and H.

title: Metallurgical-grade wafer bulk under a five-micron electronic-grade skin
idea: Minify purity to where the electrons live: grow DRAM wafer bulk from 6N upgraded-metallurgical silicon and deposit a 5 um 11N epitaxial layer on top. A buried carbon-rich gettering layer traps bulk metals during every thermal step.
why: DRAM devices use only the top few um. Polysilicon refining energy (~60 kWh/kg Siemens) and quartz demand for the bulk fall ~70-80%.

title: Eliminate the clock: asynchronous self-timed DRAM without DLLs or ODT
idea: Replace DDR's DLL, clock tree and on-die termination with a four-phase bundled-data handshake over short in-package links; each bank signals completion, so an idle interface burns nothing.
why: DLL, clocking and termination are a large share of DRAM I/O power even when idle; I/O energy falls from ~5 to <0.5 pJ/bit on short channels.

title: Cryo-trapping unreacted WF6 from CVD exhaust for on-site reuse
idea: Tungsten CVD consumes only ~20-30% of the WF6 it is fed. Condense the remainder from the foreline at -80 C (WF6 boils at 17 C) before the abatement burner, distill it free of HF and byproducts, and return it to the gas loop weekly, closing a minute-scale waste into a week-scale cycle.
why: Cuts tungsten (China ~80%) and fluorine consumption for W layers 2-4x and reduces abatement fuel energy.

title: LC-resonant adiabatic wordline drive recycles charge energy
idea: Effect: adiabatic charging, where loss is about (RC/T)*CV2. Drive wordlines from a resonant sinusoidal supply through on-interposer inductors so the 3 V swing ramps slowly relative to RC, and return the charge to the LC tank instead of dumping it to ground.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): wordline energy falls ~70%, which cuts the energy intensity of every activation.

title: Fluorocarbon-free capacitor-hole etch by cryogenic HF/water vapor
idea: Ideal: high-aspect-ratio etch with no PFAS gases. Closest: etch 60-75:1 capacitor holes at -60 to -80 C using HF + H2O/NH4F chemistry where a condensed adsorbed HF layer drives ion-assisted SiO2 removal and frozen reaction products passivate sidewalls, dropping C4F6/C4F8/CH2F2 entirely.
why: Removes PFAS-classified, high-GWP fluorocarbon etch gases ahead of EU/US PFAS restrictions; reported ~2x faster cryo etch rates also cut etch-tool capex per wafer.

title: Puller heater coils also generate the melt-damping magnetic field
idea: Combine the CZ heater and the melt-stabilizing magnet (zero masks): drive segmented heater coils with phase-shifted AC so they produce a traveling magnetic field that damps melt convection, replacing superconducting cusp magnets and their helium cryostats.
why: Helium-free magnetic CZ for 300 mm DRAM wafers; drops ~$1-2M of magnet capital per puller and magnet power.

title: Multilayer ceramic capacitor stacking for lateral 3D-DRAM storage nodes
idea: MLCC makers stack hundreds of BaTiO3 layers between nickel electrodes using abundant elements. In horizontal 3D-DRAM tiers, build each storage capacitor as an interdigitated lateral finger stack: recess the Si/SiGe superlattice sidewall, then ALD alternating TiN and paraelectric (Ba,Sr)TiO3 shells so each tier holds several parallel plates instead of one cylinder.
why: Attacks the 3D-DRAM capacitor blocker (fact 2) without 60-75:1 vertical pillar etches; thin-film BST (k ~200) can raise Cs per footprint ~3x using Ba, Sr and Ti, none of them chokepoint materials.

title: Biomineralization-style area-selective growth replaces subtractive etch steps
idea: Shells and bones place mineral only where an organic matrix tells them to. Pattern a sacrificial molecular matrix (phosphonic-acid self-assembled monolayer) once, then grow capacitor supports, hardmasks and spacers additively by area-selective ALD only on matrix-free regions, skipping blanket-deposit/litho/etch cycles.
why: Each skipped etch saves fluorocarbon gas, a mask and tool time; could remove 3-6 litho-etch steps per wafer and cut precursor waste.

title: MOF cartridges capture neon, krypton and xenon from exhaust
idea: Within $1M/24 months: package selective metal-organic-framework adsorbents (Xe/Kr-selective SBMOF-type beds plus a Ne-capture stage) into swappable cartridges on excimer-laser and etch exhausts, regenerate them offsite by temperature swing, and resell the rare gases.
why: Ne/Kr/Xe supply is tied to Russian and Ukrainian air-separation byproducts; cartridges target ~70-90% recovery for DUV lasers and etch at cartridge rather than plant capex.

title: Reverse logistics: harvest retired DIMMs into CXL pools
idea: Reverse the product flow: buy decommissioned server DIMMs, retest and re-bin the DRAM, then deploy them as pooled CXL capacity behind a controller that remaps weak rows.
why: Adds usable memory with zero new wafers, crucibles, helium or tungsten; hyperscaler retirements could supply several % of annual bit demand at a fraction of 4x-inflated contract prices.

title: Photoacoustic isotope-tracer leak detection retires helium mass spectrometers
idea: Effect: photoacoustics. A modulated mid-IR laser absorbed by a 13CO2 tracer gas creates pressure waves that a resonant MEMS microphone detects at ppb levels. 13CO2 has almost no background, so it replaces helium spraying for leak-checking vacuum chambers, gas lines and EUV/etch tools.
why: Helium: leak testing is a top-3 fab helium use; equivalent sensitivity is reached with a recyclable, abundant tracer.

title: Beach sand: MoO2 rutile template grows k-100 TiO2 without ruthenium
idea: Stimulus 'beach sand' (rutile and ilmenite grains) -> use conductive rutile-structured MoO2 from abundant U.S. molybdenum as the bottom electrode so ALD TiO2 grows epitaxially in the rutile phase (k ~100) at low temperature, as it does on RuO2, with Al doping to curb leakage.
why: Delivers the k >= 70 the capacitor wall demands while removing both ruthenium and hafnium; Ti and Mo are abundant and U.S.-sourced.

title: Po the test wafer is the product: reclaimed monitor-wafer substrates
idea: Po: 'the test wafer is the product.' Extracted: route the large stream of 200 mm monitor and dummy wafers used for tool qualification through CMP reclaim plus a thin epitaxial refresh layer, and run them as product substrates for 180 nm memory instead of virgin prime wafers.
why: Virgin polysilicon, crucible quartz and wafer energy per bit cut sharply for legacy memory; reclaim wafers cost roughly a third to a half of prime.

title: Po one cell holds four voltages: multi-level big-capacitor cells
idea: Po: 'each cell remembers a number, not a bit.' Extracted: use the large storage capacitance practical at 180 nm (30+ fF with trench or HSG capacitors) to store four charge levels (2 bits per cell), read with reference-ladder sense amplifiers and a two-step compare; refresh restores the levels.
why: Density: doubles bits per area on old tools, closing part of the 180 nm vs 12 nm gap on a depreciated domestic line, at a cost of roughly 2x row access time.

title: PCB plating-shop logic: electroless nickel-boron plugs replace tungsten contacts
idea: Circuit-board makers fill microvias with electroless metal, with no vacuum and no fluoride gases. Fill bit-line and periphery contacts bottom-up with electroless Ni-B on a NiSi seed that catalyzes deposition without scarce palladium, using suppressor additives for void-free superfill on a university plating bench.
why: Removes WF6 and tungsten (~80% China) from contacts and avoids CVD tool capex; Ni-B resistivity is higher than W but acceptable for short plugs.

title: Eliminate EUV from periodic array layers: one-master nanoimprint templates
idea: Wordline, bitline, landing-pad and storage-node layers are perfectly periodic, so write one e-beam master per layer, replicate imprint templates from it, and pattern by jet-and-flash nanoimprint, keeping DUV only for the aperiodic periphery.
why: Removes 5-7 EUV exposures (fact 4) from a single-supplier tool drawing ~1 MW each; NIL tools cost and consume roughly a tenth as much.

title: Vinyl-record stampers: nanoimprint replicates DRAM array layers without EUV
idea: Record and CD plants electroform nickel mother and stamper replicas from a single master. E-beam write one master per periodic DRAM array layer (honeycomb storage-node holes, bitline/wordline gratings), replicate hundreds of daughter templates, and pattern those layers by jet-and-flash nanoimprint at ~20 nm half-pitch.
why: Removes 2-4 of the 5-7 EUV layers (single-supplier tool; depreciation ~55% of wafer cost); imprint tools cost ~1/10 of an EUV scanner and draw a tiny fraction of its power.

title: Net-shape deposition: area-selective ALD as 3D-printing for films
idea: Additive manufacturing puts material only where the part needs it; use intrinsically chemoselective ALD (dielectric growing on TiN but blocked on SiO2 by an inhibitor vapor pulse, Ru or Mo growing only on metal) to build capacitor dielectrics, liners and caps in place, skipping blanket-deposit, litho and etch-back cycles.
why: Each skipped etch-back saves precursor that would be etched away (Hf, Zr, Ru, W utilization often <5%), a mask and fluorinated etch gas; across ~10 deposit/etch-back loops this could cut metal precursor use 30-50%.

title: Periphery first, indium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain cells last
idea: Reverse front-end order: finish CMOS periphery, then build a 2T gain-cell array in BEOL from sputtered zinc-tin-oxide (no indium, no gallium) at <400 C on top of the logic.
why: IGZO depends on indium and gallium (China ~98% of gallium); ZTO uses abundant Zn/Sn and keeps the BEOL-stacking density gain without the chokepoint metals.

title: Doped single-crystal silicon pillar as a metal-free storage electrode
idea: Periodic-table walk, Br (35): etch degenerately P-doped (>1e20 cm^-3) Si pillars with HBr/Cl2/O2 (bromide-oxide passivation, no fluorine), wrap them in ALD high-k and a TiN plate, so the pillar itself is the bottom electrode with no oxide mold, no TiN bottom electrode and no HF removal.
why: Drops ~10 steps plus the fluorocarbon etch and HF wet; stiff crystalline pillars tolerate higher AR before collapse (<=10% depletion C loss).

title: Replacement buried wordline: sacrificial poly early, aluminum fill late
idea: Combine logic's replacement-metal-gate flow with the buried wordline: a sacrificial poly-Si plug sits in the trench through the hot activation steps, then is removed and the trench filled with Al-Cu by low-temperature CVD, with all later steps (low-temp ALD capacitor) kept <=450 C.
why: Removes the largest tungsten volume in a DRAM die using abundant aluminum; lower narrow-line resistance lets wordlines double in length, cutting sub-wordline drivers in the ~49% periphery.

title: Po the transistor stands up: vertical surrounding-gate 4F2 cells
idea: Po: 'the transistor stands on its head.' Extracted: etch silicon pillars with a KrF stepper, wrap each in a gate by conformal LPCVD poly and spacer etch (Toshiba's 1988 surrounding-gate transistor), with buried diffused bitlines below and the capacitor on top, giving a 4F2 cell.
why: Density at old pitch: 4F2 vs 8F2 halves cell area, so a 180 nm U.S. line gets ~2x bits per wafer without any litho upgrade.

title: Leaf-venation loop-redundant printed interposer for HBM stacks
idea: Leaf veins form closed loops so flow routes around damage. Print panel-level RDL interposers roll-to-roll with fine copper lines arranged as looped meshes instead of single tree routes, so any printed open is bypassed, and use them in place of silicon interposers under HBM.
why: Removes the silicon interposer (wafer area, TSVs) and tolerates printing defects, cutting HBM package cost and silicon intensity.

title: Mn3Sn antiferromagnetic bit: written by torque, read by tunneling
idea: Periodic-table walk, Mn (25): store bits in the chiral spin order of the Weyl antiferromagnet Mn3Sn, switched by spin-orbit torque and read by tunneling magnetoresistance in Mn3Sn/MgO/Mn3Sn; no stray field, so cells pack without magnetic crosstalk, and THz dynamics allow sub-ns writes with magnetic-class endurance.
why: No capacitor charge wall and no refresh; only Mn and Sn, no Co, Pt or rare earths.

title: Silicon-on-nothing voids isolate cells using only silicon and hydrogen
idea: Combine isolation and body insulation via the empty-space-in-silicon effect: the one added mask etches arrays of deep holes under active-area ends, and a high-temperature H2 anneal lets silicon surface-migrate to seal them into buried voids that cut leakage paths beneath the access transistor.
why: Cuts the junction leakage tail (refresh energy ~30-50% lower) and replaces part of the STI fill oxide and its CMP with nothing but silicon and hydrogen.

title: Aquarium filter: electrodialysis skid recycles TMAH developer
idea: Stimulus 'aquarium filter' (water cycles while waste is pulled out) -> a 10-person team builds bipolar-membrane electrodialysis skids that split spent TMAH developer back into pure TMAH concentrate and clean water for reuse.
why: Cuts TMAH purchases ~80% and wastewater toxicity, easing the fab's water-treatment load.

title: Short local wordlines so abundant TiN replaces tungsten fill
idea: Ideal: a wordline with zero resistance. Work backward: make resistance irrelevant by splitting each buried wordline into 64-cell segments driven by local sub-wordline drivers placed under the array (CMOS-under-array), so all-TiN or doped-poly gates suffice and WF6 tungsten fill disappears.
why: Tungsten ~80% China, WF6 also consumes fluorine; segment RC falls ~16-64x (L squared), tolerating a 5-10x more resistive abundant conductor for ~3-5% driver area under the array.

title: Canon ELTRAN porous splitting stops grinding away 96% of HBM wafers
idea: HBM core dies are ground from 775 um to ~30 um, wasting ~96% of each Cz wafer; Canon's ELTRAN (double porous-Si layer, water-jet split) died because SOI demand was small and Smart Cut won. Grow the DRAM device epi on sealed porous silicon, process and bond it into the stack, water-jet split, and re-polish the donor for 10-20 reuses.
why: Cuts Cz silicon, polysilicon and quartz-crucible use per HBM bit ~5-10x and eliminates grinding slurry and rinse water; softens the material side of the HBM 3x-area tax.

title: Phosphate-fertilizer fluorine recovery turns fab waste into synthetic fluorspar
idea: Phosphate plants recover fluorosilicic acid and convert it to AlF3 and HF instead of mining fluorspar. Precipitate fab HF, chamber-clean and abatement fluoride as acid-grade synthetic CaF2, or route it into fluorosilicic-acid-to-HF conversion, closing the fluorine loop behind the HF, NF3 and WF6 a DRAM fab buys; the DDR/HBM product is identical.
why: Fluorspar is a critical mineral (China ~60%) underpinning every fluorine chemical in the fab; target 40-60% of fab fluorine demand from recycled feed and avoid wastewater fluoride limits.

title: Carbon-mold capacitors etched with oxygen instead of fluorocarbons
idea: Box [ZrO2 cylinder cap | Si access | voltage SA | pillar | CZ Si | O2/SO2 plasma + ash]: build the capacitor mold from amorphous carbon with nitrogen-doped carbon support bands, etch the 70:1 holes with O2/SO2 instead of C4F6/C4F8 on oxide, deposit TiN/ZrO2/TiN, then ash the mold away (no HF wet strip).
why: PFAS/PFC intensity: oxide capacitor-hole etch is one of the largest fluorocarbon users (GWP 6,000-9,000); swapping it could cut fab PFC emissions ~20-30% and the carbon etch is faster.

title: LED chip-on-board: bare DRAM die bonded directly onto DIMMs
idea: LED lighting dropped individually packaged emitters for chip-on-board arrays. Flip-chip bare DDR5 dies with redistributed bumps straight onto the RDIMM PCB, with capillary underfill and a printed conformal coat, skipping the BGA substrate, bond wires and mold compound; the module still presents a standard JEDEC DDR5 edge, SPD and RCD.
why: Removes gold/copper wire, supply-constrained BT laminate substrates and solder balls per die, shrinking module material ~30% with no host change.

title: Eliminate lithography for the cell layer: self-ordered anodic alumina template
idea: Deposit aluminium over the array and anodize it in oxalic or sulfuric acid; hexagonal pores self-order at 25-60 nm pitch with aspect ratios above 1000:1. One coarse imprint of pit seeds pins pore registry to the periphery, the pores host capacitors or vertical channels, and the alumina stays as the dielectric.
why: Removes EUV/multipatterning and high-AR plasma etch for the cell layer, using abundant Al and dilute acid; makes AR>115 capacitors trivial (fact 1).

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores as a plasma-free capacitor mold
idea: Periodic-table walk, Al+O (13,8): deposit 2-3 um Al over the array, nano-imprint pore seeds aligned to storage-node contacts, and anodize in oxalic/sulfuric acid so vertical pores self-grow at AR >100; open the barrier in H3PO4 and ALD the electrode/dielectric stack inside.
why: Replaces the C4F8/CHF3 high-aspect-ratio oxide etch (the most fluorine- and capital-intensive DRAM step) with room-temperature electrochemistry; AR 100+ gives ~7 fF.

title: Spin-crossover iron complexes store bits inside thermal hysteresis loops
idea: Effect: Fe(II)-triazole coordination polymers switch between low-spin and high-spin states with a 20-40 K wide thermal hysteresis loop near room temperature. Nano-cells held at the loop center are flipped by a local Joule pulse and read through their 10-30% change in permittivity or conductance; there is no stored charge to leak.
why: Refresh (fact 3) and Hf/W/capacitor-etch dependence; uses only Fe, C, N, H, so no scarce element is involved.

title: Hydrogen backside cooling shares the fab forming-gas recycle loop
idea: Combine the chuck's backside-cooling gas with the fab's existing H2 supply: run 5-15 Torr H2 (thermal conductivity ~0.18 W/m-K vs He ~0.15) under wafers in etch/CVD, recapture it through a palladium-membrane purifier and return it to the forming-gas anneal header.
why: Eliminates the largest in-fab helium use while Qatar's ~30% is offline; equal or better heat transfer; H2 can be electrolyzed on site in the U.S.

title: Hydrogen backside cooling replaces helium in every wafer chuck
idea: Minify helium to zero: swap the He backside gas in etch and CVD electrostatic chucks for on-site electrolytic H2 at 5-15 Torr, which conducts heat about 20% better than He. Per-chuck flows are under 0.1 slm and are N2-diluted in the vacuum exhaust, so they stay far below flammability limits.
why: Backside cooling is the largest single helium use in a DRAM fab. Removing it cuts fab He demand ~60-70% and the exposure to the Qatar outage (~30% of supply), using an abundant, US-producible gas.

title: Eliminate helium backside cooling: closed-loop hydrogen chuck gas
idea: Etch and implant chucks flow He at 5-20 Torr behind the wafer; swap it for H2 (thermal conductivity 0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K), confined by a sealed ceramic land, recaptured through a Pd-membrane purifier and recirculated, with chamber H2 sensors interlocked well below the lower explosive limit.
why: Backside cooling is a top fab helium use while Qatar's ~30% of supply is offline; cuts fab He draw 50-80% with equal or better wafer temperature control.

title: Hydrogen backside cooling replaces helium in every chuck
idea: Inverts 'helium is the only safe backside heat-transfer gas': feed electrostatic chucks in etch/CVD/implant with 5-20 Torr hydrogen (thermal conductivity higher than He) from an on-site electrolyzer, recirculated through a palladium-membrane loop with sub-LEL leak sensing; the backside gas never touches plasma.
why: Backside cooling is one of the largest fab helium uses; removes dependence on Qatar (~30%, offline since March 2026) for that load; H2 is made from water and power on site.

title: Party balloon: per-pump helium harvest-and-repurify loop
idea: Random stimulus 'party balloon' (helium that silently leaks away) -> treat every dry-pump exhaust as a leaking balloon. A compact hollow-fiber membrane stage plus cold-trap/getter polisher on each etch and implant pump exhaust pulls backside-cooling helium out of the N2 ballast at >90% recovery, repurifies it to 6N and feeds it back to the chucks.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30% of supply offline): cuts fab helium purchases ~70-85% and buffers supply shocks at minor energy cost.

title: Welding torch: bolt-on hydrogen backside-cooling kit for etch chucks
idea: Stimulus 'welding torch' (hydrogen handled safely every day) -> a 10-person team assembles a bolt-on kit (small PEM electrolyzer, palladium purifier, mass-flow controller, H2 sensors and interlocks) that swaps 5-20 Torr helium backside gas for hydrogen (0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K) on existing electrostatic chucks.
why: Eliminates helium from its largest fab use; H2 is made on demand from water and power, and the kit is built from catalog parts.

title: Dilution-fridge-grade helium recapture ring on every etch chuck
idea: Quantum-computing labs recover >95% of helium boil-off; copy them by adding an edge-scavenging vacuum ring around each electrostatic chuck that captures backside-cooling helium leakage and feeds a tool-side membrane purifier and compressor returning 99.999% He to the chuck line. A fab helium 'bank' meters per-tool recovery the way a cryo lab does.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30% offline since March 2026): cuts fab He purchases ~80-90% with small capex and protects etch/CVD uptime.

title: Rocket-test-stand hydrogen as backside wafer coolant instead of helium
idea: Rocket engine test stands handle hydrogen routinely, and H2 conducts heat better than He (0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K). Run chuck backside cooling on 5-20 Torr electrolytic H2 (or H2/Ar) with leak-tight seals, H2 sensors and dilution exhaust, qualifying each etch chemistry for H-radical side effects.
why: Removes the largest fab helium use in etch and deposition; H2 is made domestically on site from water and power, with equal or better wafer temperature control.

title: Glassblower makes crucibles from polysilicon plants' waste chloride
idea: Persona: a fiber-optic glassblower. Flame-hydrolyze silicon tetrachloride, the unavoidable byproduct of U.S. Siemens polysilicon plants, onto a rotating graphite mandrel (the outside-vapor-deposition method used for fiber). Sinter the 99.9999% synthetic silica soot into crucibles with an Al-doped outer layer for creep stiffness.
why: Turns a Michigan and Washington waste stream into a Spruce Pine substitute. Metal impurities ~100x below natural HPQ.

title: Conformal graphite-foil chuck membrane cools wafers without backside gas
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics (a rigid chuck becomes compliant): face the chuck with a thin compliant pyrolytic-graphite or CNT-forest membrane that electrostatic force flattens against the wafer backside. Heat then flows through solid contact instead of through He-filled grooves.
why: Removes backside helium, the largest fab He use, entirely without the safety work that H2 needs. Uses only C on an AlN/Al2O3 chuck body.

title: Johnsen-Rahbek solid-contact chuck conducts heat with zero backside gas
idea: Contact conductance h ~ 1.25 k_s (m/sigma)(P/H)^0.95 grows with true contact area; a Johnsen-Rahbek chuck gives ~10x the clamp pressure of a Coulomb chuck, and a compliant 50 um pyrolytic-graphite skin raises true contact from ~0.1% to a few percent, reaching gas-gap-class 500-1000 W/m2K with no gas.
why: Removes helium entirely from chucks, including cryogenic etch where He cooling is critical; backside particle and carbon contamination control is the risk.

title: Jacquard loom lithography: Texas-made DLP mirrors write periphery layers
idea: The Jacquard loom replaced fixed patterns with programmable punched cards; build maskless exposure engines from Dallas-made DLP micromirror chips with reduction optics and expose DRAM periphery, pad, redistribution and upper-metal layers straight from data.
why: Removes masks and blanks for ~20-30 non-critical layers per product and foreign stepper dependence on those layers, and lets each wafer carry its own repair and redundancy wiring; ~0.3-1 um resolution suffices there.

title: Po crucible made of ice: cold-copper skull-melt Czochralski silicon
idea: Po: 'the crucible is made of ice.' Extracted: pull 300 mm CZ ingots from a melt held in a water-cooled segmented copper crucible, where induction heating levitates and stirs the melt and a frozen silicon skull is the only wall contact, so no high-purity quartz crucible is consumed and no oxygen dissolves from silica walls; a cusp magnetic field damps convection for radial dopant uniformity.
why: Removes the Spruce Pine (>80%) high-purity-quartz crucible chokepoint for DRAM substrates; low-oxygen wafers also remove oxygen-precipitate leakage sites in the retention tail. Cost is ~2-3x melt power per ingot.

title: MEMS-release vapor HF replaces wet buffered-oxide etch and rinses
idea: MEMS makers release structures with anhydrous vapor HF and an alcohol catalyst, using no liquids. Replace wet BOE/DHF oxide strips with vapor HF in a university fab, recovering HF in a closed cylinder loop, and quantify selectivity to nitride and residues.
why: Cuts HF wastewater, rinse UPW and fluoride sludge per wafer, which matters most at water-scarce U.S. sites.

title: Microbiologist farms magnetotactic bacteria for ready-made magnetite bits
idea: Persona: a microbiologist whose magnetotactic bacteria grow chains of uniform 45 nm magnetite crystals at room temperature. Harvest the magnetosomes and align them by field into lithography-free pockets on a CMOS crossbar. Read each half-metallic Fe3O4 crystal by tunnel magnetoresistance through a thin ALD barrier.
why: Single-domain non-volatile bits made from iron and sugar water, with no Co or Pt sputter targets, at low fabrication energy.

title: Monolayer doping forms damage-free access-transistor junctions
idea: Box [standard cap | RCAT Si with molecular-monolayer-doped junctions | standard | standard | Si | allylboronic or allylphosphonate SAM + oxide cap + N2 spike anneal]: replace beamline implants at the storage-node junction with self-assembled dopant molecules driven in by RTP, giving abrupt sub-5 nm junctions with no implant point defects.
why: Implant damage seeds the trap-assisted leakage tail; damage-free junctions could cut tail GIDL ~3-10x, which means less refresh, and remove implanter plasma-flood gas use.

title: Molecular monolayer doping replaces arsine and phosphine implants
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero toxic hydride gases and no implanter for cell junctions. Graft a self-assembled monolayer of phosphorus- or boron-bearing molecules onto silicon, cap it with oxide and spike-anneal to drive a sub-5 nm conformal junction, which also works on the sidewalls of lateral 3D-DRAM channels that beamline implants cannot reach.
why: Removes concentrated AsH3/PH3/BF3 supply chains and ~$5-10M implanters per layer; conformal doping unblocks lateral transistors, a key 3D-DRAM blocker.

title: Blacksmith nitrides manganese into a racetrack memory
idea: Persona: a blacksmith who case-hardens steel with nitrogen. Reactively sputter ferrimagnetic Mn4N, which has perpendicular anisotropy and low magnetization. Tune it near angular-momentum compensation with Ni substitution so that current drives domain walls at ~1 km/s along vertical racetracks.
why: Non-volatile, with many bits per access transistor, which cuts periphery and area per bit. No Co, Pt, Gd or Tb.

title: Substitute CVD silicon carbide for quartz furnace ware and chamber rings
idea: Replace quartz diffusion tubes, wafer boats, liners and etch focus rings with CVD-SiC, sintered Y2O3 or single-crystal-silicon parts that are re-coated in place by plasma spray or CVD when eroded, so parts are refurbished rather than scrapped.
why: Quartzware is the second-largest high-purity-quartz draw after crucibles; 5-10x longer part life cuts quartz demand and particle-driven yield loss.

title: Tin-oxide rutile template grows k~90 TiO2 capacitors without Ru
idea: Rutile TiO2 has k~90-170 but only forms rutile at DRAM temperatures on a rutile-structured template, today RuO2 (Ru ~90% South Africa). Use conductive Sb:SnO2 or metallic MoO2 (rutile family, ~2-3% mismatch) as bottom-electrode template and 2-5% Al-doped TiO2 to raise the leakage barrier.
why: Fact 1 asks for k~70: doubling k from ZrO2's ~40 halves the 60-75:1 aspect ratio for the same Cs, and removes Zr/Hf ALD and ruthenium; Sn, Mo, Ti are diversified or US-sourced.

title: Fab that breathes with the grid: buffer WIP to follow cheap power
idea: Inverts 'a fab runs flat out 24/7': size work-in-progress buffers in front of the most energy-hungry steps (epitaxy, furnaces, CVD, abatement burners, chillers) so they run hard during curtailed solar/wind hours and idle at peaks, add chilled-water thermal storage, and schedule with a cycle-time vs $/MWh co-optimizer.
why: Shifting ~30% of fab load to curtailed power cuts electricity cost ~20-30% and makes renewable-rich US regions viable fab sites.

title: Topcoat-free immersion resist via self-segregating siloxane additive
idea: Combine resist and immersion topcoat (zero masks): a hydrocarbon-siloxane block additive floats to the resist surface during spin coat and forms the hydrophobic water barrier normally made by fluorinated topcoats and fluorinated surface additives.
why: Removes PFAS-class topcoats and one coat/bake step from 10+ ArF immersion layers per DRAM wafer ahead of PFAS restrictions.

title: Astronomy CCD shift-register memory for streaming KV-cache reads
idea: Astronomers' CCDs move charge packets with >99.9999% transfer efficiency using only polysilicon gates over oxide, with no per-cell contacts or metal capacitors. KV-cache reads are long sequential streams, so build CCD loop memories with sense amps every few thousand stages, ~4F2 cells, and refresh by circulation.
why: Eliminates per-cell W contacts and high-k capacitor stacks and shrinks periphery (fact 7); materials and cost per bit may be ~2-3x lower for streaming tiers.

title: Po broken chips are the product: bank-salvage CXL memory
idea: Po: 'sell only the broken chips.' Extracted: dies that fail final test because of one or two dead banks or a slow mat, scrapped or downgraded today, are packaged with a small CXL controller that keeps a per-die bank map and presents a contiguous address space, priced per good GB.
why: Yield and resource intensity: recovers several percent of wafer output whose wafer, helium, crucible and EUV cost is already sunk; strongest for HBM-class dies with 20-30% lower yield.

title: Strippable absorber mask blanks cycled through multiple reuses
idea: Worsen: scrap synthetic-quartz mask blanks at every DRAM node and every pattern ECO. Flip: design blanks with a sacrificial etch-stop under the absorber stack so it strips cleanly, then re-polish and re-coat the quartz substrate, cycling each blank 3-5 times.
why: Synthetic quartz and mask-shop capacity: DRAM uses ~60-80 masks per node, so blank demand falls ~3x.

title: Squirrel scatter-hoarding: distributed national reserves of fab chokepoint materials
idea: Grey squirrels scatter-hoard across hundreds of small caches so no single loss is fatal. Policy: tie CHIPS incentives to every US memory fab holding 90-day rotating caches of helium (ISO dewars), HPQ crucibles, WF6 and Hf precursors, with a pooled inter-fab lending rule during outages, instead of one central stockpile.
why: Turns a Qatar-style helium outage or a Spruce Pine disruption from months of lost output into a short hiccup, protecting utilization when depreciation is ~55% of wafer cost.

title: Eliminate TSVs and solder: inductive-coupling links between thinned dies
idea: Stack ~20 um thinned DRAM dies with vertically aligned on-chip spiral coils, passing data by near-field inductive coupling and delivering power through a few large vias or edge rails.
why: Removes most copper TSVs, Sn-Ag microbumps and keep-out zones behind HBM's ~3x area tax (fact 6); ~0.1 pJ/bit versus 3-4 pJ/bit.

title: Silicon-carbide access transistors make DRAM cells nearly non-leaking
idea: Box [MIM cap | 4H-SiC trench MOSFET (3.26 eV gap) | Si voltage SA | array-on-periphery hybrid bond | 200 mm SiC wafers from the EV supply chain | DUV litho]: build the cell array on SiC, where intrinsic carrier density is ~1e-8 cm-3 versus 1e10 for Si, so junction and GIDL leakage collapse, then bond it onto a Si periphery wafer.
why: Leakage tail/refresh (~46 fJ/bit): retention goes from 64 ms toward hours, refresh nearly vanishes and Cs can drop to ~1 fF (shallower caps, less ZrO2/TiN/etch gas); uses fast-growing US SiC wafer capacity instead of HPQ-crucible CZ.

title: Sonic-film memory: strain pulses address bits instead of transistors
idea: Revive Sperry's 1960s sonic-film memory: an AlN transducer launches a GHz strain pulse along a magnetostrictive Fe-Co strip, and a global current pulse writes only where the strain pulse is at that instant (magnetoelastic coincidence). The inverse effect reads the bit back, so a bit's location is set by time of flight.
why: No EUV, no per-bit transistors and no decoders (fact 7: periphery); no Hf or W; addressing logic shrinks to timers; claims 5x less periphery area per bit.

title: Eliminate the data highway: dot-product units in each mat's sense-amp stripe
idea: Put an 8-bit column-serial MAC tree in every mat's sense-amp stripe so weights stay in the row buffer, activations are broadcast in, and only partial sums leave the bank.
why: Data never crosses the die or the I/O: ~4 pJ/bit effective drops to ~0.3 pJ/bit, and fewer HBM stacks (TSV copper, 3x area) are needed for the same throughput.

title: Thrift store: CXL cards giving retired DIMMs second lives
idea: Stimulus 'thrift store' -> a 10-person team designs and contract-assembles CXL Type-3 expander cards with DIMM slots on a merchant CXL controller, plus a burn-in and retention sorter, so hyperscalers redeploy decommissioned DDR4/DDR5 as a far-memory tier.
why: Each reused GB is a GB of wafer, helium, water and energy not spent; millions of DIMMs retire yearly with life left, adding supply during the 4x price spike.

title: Rare-earth-free motor magnet chemistry for platinum-free MRAM
idea: EV-motor makers are replacing NdFeB with iron nitride (Fe16N2) and synthetic tetrataenite (L10-FeNi). Adapt these phases as the perpendicular free and reference layers of a spin-torque cell, removing Pt/Co multilayers, the Ir in the synthetic antiferromagnet and heavy Ta seeds.
why: MRAM is capacitor-free with very high endurance but leans on Pt, Ir, Ru and Ta (South Africa/Russia/DRC chokepoints). Iron and nitrogen are everywhere.

title: Iron-silicon Heusler electrodes for cobalt-free, platinum-free magnetic tunnel junctions
idea: Periodic-table walk, Fe (26): grow D03 Fe3Si (or Fe2MnSi) epitaxial electrodes on MgO, couple synthetic antiferromagnets through Cr instead of Ru, and pin with MnN antiferromagnets instead of PtMn/IrMn.
why: Swaps Co (DRC), Pt/Ir (South Africa) and Ru for Fe, Si, Mn, Cr, N in any spin-based DRAM substitute; abundant-only magnetic stack.

title: Zero scrap: every die sold with its error map
idea: Reverse yield accounting: instead of discarding dies that fail repair, grade all dies by measured raw BER up to 1% and sell them as error-mapped memory for ECC-heavy AI inference tiers.
why: Turns 10-20% scrapped dies (and HBM's 20-30% yield loss) into supply; the same wafers, crucibles and helium give more sellable bits.

title: Zettacore's redox molecules reused as DRAM storage nodes, not nonvolatile bits
idea: Zettacore's porphyrin memory died chasing nonvolatile retention through a 400 C back-end. Use the molecules where retention is cheap: graft a multi-redox monolayer (ferrocene-porphyrin triads, 2-4 electrons per molecule at ~1e14 molecules/cm2) as the last step onto a short ~10:1 TiN cup, so faradaic charge (~30 uC/cm2) supplies the 5 fF-equivalent storage that today needs a 60-75:1 pillar.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall: ~6x shorter storage node, no ZrO2/HfO2 high-k, fewer fluorocarbon deep-etch steps; molecules are C, H, N, Fe; refresh already exists so molecular retention limits do not matter. Electron-transfer speed is the risk.

title: Seltzer: supercritical CO2 drying saves tall pillars and rinse water
idea: Stimulus 'seltzer' (CO2 dissolved under pressure) -> after capacitor-mold removal, exchange the rinse liquid for supercritical CO2 with a co-solvent so no liquid-vapor meniscus can topple tall pillars, and use scCO2 plus chelator cleans for post-etch residue.
why: Pillar leaning caps aspect ratio; zero capillary force allows >100:1 pillars while cutting UPW and IPA per clean ~80%, with CO2 recycled.

title: Inside-out fab: the cleanroom is a tube, not a ballroom
idea: Reverse which volume is clean: wafers never leave sealed N2/vacuum tube transport and docked tools, while people and the building air stay at ordinary grade.
why: Cleanroom HVAC/HEPA is a large share of fab energy and capital; shrinking the clean volume ~100x could cut fab facility energy ~30-40% and building capex.

title: Vacuum-gap floating gate: flash physics without oxide wear
idea: Inverts 'a floating gate needs an oxide tunnel barrier, which wears out': suspend the floating node over a sealed 2-3 nm vacuum gap and charge it by Fowler-Nordheim field emission across vacuum with ~8 V local pulses; vacuum holds no traps to damage, so endurance is effectively unlimited, and at read fields emission is nil, so retention lasts years.
why: Zero refresh, nonvolatile, unlimited-endurance cell from Si, SiO2 and TiN only, with no high-k or Hf.

title: Sealed vacuum-gap bitlines let a quarter-sized capacitor suffice
idea: Bitline capacitance is mostly coupling through k~4-7 spacers; vacuum (k=1) gaps made by depositing a sacrificial carbon spacer, sealing it and ashing it out through a porous cap cut CBL ~3-4x, so the same signal needs ~1/4 the cell charge.
why: A quarter of Cs lets 3D lateral capacitors use plain Al2O3 (no Zr/Hf) at 1/4 the length; with 40 tiers that is ~10x density at equal cost. Air is the cheapest dielectric there is.

title: Fiddlehead-rolled foil memory: square metres coiled into a cartridge
idea: Ferns pack a large frond into a tight coil. Print indium-free Zn-Sn-O TFT gain-cell arrays (~10 um2 cells) roll-to-roll on 25 um polyimide, then coil ~30 m2 into a 1 L cylinder with edge-bonded flex taps every 10 cm feeding a silicon controller behind a CXL port.
why: At ~$30-50 per processed m2 this could reach ~$3-5/GB with no EUV, no Cz wafers and no helium-intensive etch; ~100 ns-1 us latency suits a capacity tier and opens a new supply line.

title: Satellite-lidar solid-state 193 nm source frees lithography from neon
idea: Spaceborne UV instruments cannot carry gas bottles, so they use frequency-multiplied solid-state lasers. Build a 193 nm source from a high-power Yb fiber laser and an OPO mixed through a CLBO sum-frequency cascade, sized for non-critical ArF-dry and periphery layers.
why: Excimer lasers depend on neon and krypton, historically ~50% from Ukraine/Russia: this removes rare-gas consumption and laser-gas refill downtime.

title: Anodic electrochemical growth of capacitor dielectric replaces ALD precursors
idea: Worsen: build every capacitor dielectric atom by atom with costly, slow, single-sourced ALD precursors in vacuum tools. Flip: deposit a thin Ti or Ta-Ti electrode liner, then grow a barrier-type anodic TiO2/Ta2O5 dielectric electrochemically at room temperature in a wet cell. Anodic growth is self-limiting and conformal at any aspect ratio, with thickness set by voltage (~2 nm/V).
why: Precursor intensity, ALD capital and the high-AR conformality wall: low-capex wet tools with abundant metals, and a k ~40-80 dielectric with no Hf/Zr.

title: Tungsten closed loop from chamber shields and scrubber residues
idea: Worsen: let 70-90% of WF6 tungsten end up on chamber walls, in scrubbers and in sludge. Flip: line W CVD chambers with removable collection shields, oxidize the shield and scrubber tungsten into soluble tungstate, refine it to ammonium paratungstate and re-fluorinate it to WF6 domestically.
why: Tungsten (~80% China) and low CVD utilization: the loop could cut virgin W demand ~50-70%.

title: Dopant-selective porous silicon replaces SiGe sacrificial layers in 3D DRAM
idea: SiGe/Si superlattices are strain-limited (mismatch accumulates, capping ~60-100 tiers) and need germanium. Grow a zero-mismatch superlattice of p+ (1e19 B) and lightly doped Si below 600 C, then anodize in HF: holes concentrate in p+ layers, turning only them into mesoporous Si (>100:1 selectivity), which is oxidized into inter-tier isolation.
why: No strain ceiling, so 200+ crystalline-Si tiers come from one epi run and one wet step: >=10x density at roughly today's wafer cost, with no germanium (China ~60%+).

title: Back-end oxide CMOS latches: static memory stacked over logic
idea: Inverts 'static memory must live in the silicon substrate': build cross-coupled latches from n-type amorphous ZnO and p-type SnO/Cu2O thin-film transistors in the metal stack at <350 C, several tiers high, with wide-gap leakage below 1e-18 A per device.
why: Zero refresh with standby ~1000x below silicon SRAM; abundant Zn, Sn and Cu; no substrate area or capacitor materials.

title: Eliminate the ballroom cleanroom: sealed-pod mini-environment fab
idea: Wafers never meet room air: every tool docks sealed nitrogen pods and the building is held only at ISO 8, so HVAC is sized for people, not particles, enabling small modular U.S. memory fabs.
why: Cleanroom HVAC is ~30-50% of fab electricity and a large share of shell capital; cuts both and shortens build time.

title: Germanium-free 3D DRAM stacks using boron-doped silicon sacrificial layers
idea: Ideal: 3D tiers grown from silicon alone. Closest: grow the multi-tier epitaxial stack as alternating undoped Si and heavily boron-doped Si (or Si:C) instead of Si/SiGe, and remove sacrificial layers laterally by dopant-selective electrochemical porosification + oxidation or doping-selective wet etch.
why: Germanium (China ~60%+, export-controlled since 2023) is the default 3D DRAM sacrificial layer; Si/Si:B also removes lattice mismatch, allowing >100 tiers without relaxation defects (Fact 2).

title: Ceria-free shallow-trench planarization by selective dry etch-back
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero rare-earth ceria slurry and no CMP water. Fill isolation trenches with flowable oxide, then planarize with a self-limiting, nitride-stopping remote-plasma etch-back under optical endpoint control instead of ceria-slurry CMP.
why: Ceria is a China-concentrated rare earth and CMP is a major slurry and UPW consumer; dry etch-back also reduces dishing and particle defects, removing one chokepoint per STI layer.

title: Clotting-capsule self-healing printed interconnect raises foil-memory yield
idea: Blood clots seal wounds automatically. Embed 5 um microcapsules of copper-formate ink in the printed dielectric over the lines; a crack ruptures them and the released ink, reduced to copper by local Joule heating from a test current, bridges the open line.
why: Printed lines fail open from cracks and particles; self-repair could lift array yield from ~90% to >99%, cutting scrap and making large-area memory economical.

title: Paint-pigment TiCl4 refined into electronic capacitor electrodes
idea: As sugar refiners turn table sugar into pharmaceutical sucrose, add a fractional-distillation and adsorber polishing train beside U.S. chloride-process pigment plants in Tennessee and Mississippi to make 6N TiCl4 for TiN capacitor electrodes, gate liners and barriers.
why: TiN is in every DRAM capacitor and wordline; this gives a domestic electrode supply at commodity cost, removing imported TiCl4/TDMAT and the pull toward scarce ruthenium electrodes.

title: Ceria-free planarization using UV-photocatalytic titania polishing pads
idea: Ideal: polishing with light instead of rare earths. Closest: embed anatase TiO2 in the CMP pad and illuminate through a transparent platen; photogenerated holes oxidize and soften Si/SiN/oxide surfaces so a dilute colloidal-silica slurry removes them, replacing CeO2 slurries in STI and ILD steps.
why: Semiconductor ceria is mostly Chinese rare-earth supply; also cuts slurry volume and wastewater across DRAM's dozens of CMP steps.

title: Anodized aluminum self-ordered pores form capacitor molds
idea: Worsen: lithographically print and plasma-etch billions of capacitor holes per die. Flip: deposit thick aluminum, pre-texture it with a coarse imprint and anodize it. The Al2O3 self-organizes into hexagonal pores with AR >500 at a pitch set by voltage (~2.5 nm/V), and those pores become the capacitor mold, so no capacitor etch tool is needed.
why: Capacitor AR wall, PFAS etch gases and etch capital: Al is abundant in the U.S. and AR 100+ comes easily. The hard parts are reaching ~40 nm pitch and registering to the storage nodes.

title: Po the chip is mostly air: air-gap bitlines shrink capacitors
idea: Po: 'the chip is mostly air.' Extracted: after patterning bitlines, cap them with non-conformal PECVD oxide that pinches off above the spaces, leaving air (k ~1) between neighbors; bitline capacitance falls ~40%, so the same sense signal needs ~40% less storage capacitance.
why: Capacitor charge wall: signal depends on Cs/Cb, so lower Cb allows shorter, cheaper capacitors and cuts bitline CV2 energy ~30-40%.

title: Embrace random wiring: self-assembled crossbars mapped after fabrication
idea: Ideal: wiring that costs nothing because nobody designs it. Closest: grow dense random or partly ordered nanoline crossbars (dewetting, DSA) with a cell wherever lines cross; reach lines through a coarse-litho stochastic decoder (randomly doped address wires, Lieber/DeHon style) and run a one-time BIST discovery pass that writes a per-chip address-translation table.
why: 100x: shifts cost from lithographic precision to cheap logic and test time; if 30-50% of random cells are usable, $/GB falls ~100x versus precision-patterned arrays. Trades ~1-3% map overhead and variable capacity per die.

title: Po memory made of sandpaper: silicon-carbide refresh-free DRAM
idea: Po: 'memory made of sandpaper.' Extracted: build 1T1C cells in 4H silicon carbide (carborundum) on 150 mm SiC lines with >=0.5 um tools; the 3.2 eV bandgap cuts thermal generation leakage so cells hold charge for hours to years at room temperature, as 1990s SiC DRAM experiments showed.
why: Refresh eliminated (fact 3) and U.S. manufacturability (SiC fabs in NC and NY); density is low but energy per bit for refresh-free working memory drops sharply.
